rotation_note: Unattended-run override: NO rotating subset. All 3 core keywords plus the entire politics pool (34 keywords, grouped into geopolitics / policy_regulation / elections_public_opinion) are working keywords today (37 total). Day-of-year 322 sets ORDER only: group lead rotates so no group leads twice in a row (elections_public_opinion led 11-17, so geopolitics leads today, then policy_regulation, then elections_public_opinion); within each group the list starts at offset 322 % group_size in pool order (geopolitics 10 -> 2: sovereign AI first; policy 15 -> 7: AI safety institute first; elections 9 -> 7: 딥페이크 선거 first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-17, so items published 11-17 (after the prior harvest) through 11-18 are in scope. Context: Wednesday 11-18 in Korea / Tuesday 11-17 in the US and EU at harvest time — expect US agency releases, court orders and Federal Register public-inspection items dated 11-17, EU Tuesday items, plus Korean Wednesday ministry releases dated 11-18 (day before 수능). Hooks this week — only official documents are new, skip previews: House closed briefing with Jensen Huang on 11-18 US time (probably after harvest; only its outcome, a subpoena, or a bill markup is new); APEC Shenzhen US-China summit 11-18..19 (only a signed joint statement / AI channel text is new); CCW 7th Review Conference Geneva 11-16..20 (only adopted decisions, formal working papers or national statements posted by UNODA are new); 수능 11-19 (the 11-16 차관회의 measures are covered — only a final 교육부 device-ban/Wi-Fi-block notice text with new terms, or an actual 수능-day AI-device incident with official action, is new); Meta AI-scraping terms take effect 11-20 (only a new regulator/court order is new); 중기부 모두의 창업 AI vendor audit due 11-20 (only results/sanctions are new). The Commerce remote-access chip rule (covered 11-17) — its Federal Register publication is the SAME story unless it adds new terms (country list, thresholds) not in the 11-17 card. In scope: bills introduced/marked up, agency rules/bulletins, court rulings and filings, regulator enforcement, export-control actions, official after-action reports on AI-enabled interference, platform takedown reports. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, commentary without a new document. Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
